what_happened: On a STRAIGHT command (turning to RIGHT at the end), the policy's planned path pulled left away from the recorded path at about 9.6–11 m/s. The ego drifted into the adjacent left lane and side-swiped actor 33, which was driving alongside it. The lead car was still about 16 m ahead, so the lead was not the problem.

After the intersection, the ego drove along the left edge of the street, about 1.8 m left of the recorded path, at a steady 4.5–5 m/s. Its front clipped car 68, which was parked on the left (the dark Audi in the camera), and it never slowed down. This is a sideswipe of a parked car caused by bad lateral positioning, not a lead vehicle in its lane. A rear contact also happened, but it came after the at-fault front collision.

At a junction where the route called for a right turn, the policy planned a path straight ahead and then curving left across the tram tracks, ignoring the right turn. The ego veered left out of its lane and left the drivable area about 1 s after handoff. No actor was nearby; the car ahead was about 30 m away and pulling away.

After handoff, the ego was going about 8 m/s toward the intersection with the command STRAIGHT, which changed to RIGHT at the end. It steered left out of its lane instead, into the next lane where actor 33 was driving alongside, and hit it with its front-left (collision_front). The vehicle ahead stayed about 19–21 m away the whole time, so the crash came from the policy's unprompted swerve left, not from a vehicle ahead.

Approaching the intersection stop line at about 4.5 m/s, the ego was flagged offroad at 6.0 s. It was only about 0.5 m from the recorded human path, and on the map it still looks to be inside the lane area. The policy's plan was bending left/straight across the intersection while the route turns right, but the route command showed STRAIGHT until 6.0 s. At failure the ego had barely moved off the human line, so the offroad flag may be a borderline edge-of-drivable-area call rather than a real excursion.

The route command was RIGHT, but the ego instead steered left across the lanes toward a gas station lot, about 5 to 6 m/s. At 9.7 s it crossed the road boundary into the lot, 14 m from the recorded human path, without hitting anything.

The route command was RIGHT, but the ego stayed in the far-left lane and kept drifting left away from the recorded path, which went right. At about 10 m/s it went over the left edge onto the landscaped median by the tree, 6.3 m off the recording. No other actor was close.

Coming out of the intersection at about 4.8 m/s, the ego kept its planned path on the far left of the road instead of following the human path to the right. It drove into the front corner of parked car 68 on the left curb without braking or steering away.

With a RIGHT command, the ego cut the right turn far too early, about 14 m from the recorded path. It left the lanes at the corner and drove at about 5 m/s into the gas-station lot, where it was flagged offroad at 9.4 s. There was no collision.

The route command was RIGHT and the route went right, but after handoff the policy kept steering left. It crossed the left lanes and went up onto the planted median, where it hit a palm tree and left the road at 8.7s, 6.2 m from the recorded path. There was no lead vehicle close by (the gap was 24 m or more), and the camera view was clean before the drift.

At 6.0 s the ego was crossing the stop line into the intersection at about 4.5 m/s when the offroad flag tripped. It was only 0.5 m from the human's path, and nothing was close ahead. The policy's plan was bending left/straight while the route turns right, and the camera command only switched from STRAIGHT to RIGHT at the failure frame. But the ego hadn't yet moved off the human's line in any visible way, so the offroad call may come from the map's lane edge at the intersection entry rather than a real departure.

The route said to turn RIGHT, but after handoff the ego kept going at about 12 m/s and drifted left toward the double-yellow centre line, about 7.8 m off the recorded path. Its planned path veered left into the lane of actor 85, which looks like an oncoming car (the gap closed from 17.7 m to 2.9 m in 0.5 s), and the ego hit it side-on at 9.0 s.

While going straight through the intersection at about 10 m/s, the ego's planned path (orange) bent left out of its lane. The ego drifted into the left lane and side-swiped vehicle 33, which was driving alongside it on the left (collision_lateral at 6.9s). The lead car was still about 16 m ahead, so this was not a following-distance problem.

Approaching the intersection at about 10 m/s, the policy's plan veered left of the recorded path into the adjacent left lane. At 7.0 s the ego sideswiped actor 33, which was travelling beside it in that lane (a lateral collision); the gap to the lead car was still about 16 m.

After handoff, the ego left its routed right-hand lane and drifted left into the curbside lane of parked cars (31, 6, 3), while the planned route went right. It kept going at about 11–12 m/s as the gap to parked car 6 shrank from 45 m to 4 m, barely slowed, and hit car 6 with its front.

After crossing the intersection, the ego's plan bent left toward the curb, away from the right-hand lane path. Holding about 4.7 m/s and never braking, it hit the front of parked car 68, a black Audi at the left curb, as the gap closed from 23 m to 4 m. The camera view was clean until impact, and the rear contact flagged in the data is not visible in the frames.

After the handoff at 4.6 s, the ego drifted left out of its travel lane and into the parked-car strip on the left curb, though the route was RIGHT and its own plan followed the lane. It held about 11–12 m/s and drove front-first into parked car 6 (the gap shrank from 45 m to 4 m with almost no braking), ending offroad about 3.2 m from the human's path. The camera view looked clean until the impact.

The route command was RIGHT, but the ego went off the recorded path at about 6 m/s, cutting across the corner and steering up and to the left toward the gas-station lot. Its planned path (orange) pointed off the road, and it crossed the road edge at 9.6 s, about 14 m from the human trajectory, with no actor involved.

The policy took over at 4.7 s as the ego approached the intersection at about 4.4 m/s. Its planned path drifted left and then bent toward the left side of the junction, even though the route turns right (the command changes to RIGHT by 6.0 s). At 6.0 s the ego was flagged offroad at the stop line while only 0.5 m from where the human drove, so it barely clipped the road edge and may have hit a map-boundary artifact.

After the 4.6 s handoff, the ego held about 13–14 m/s and drifted left toward the parked cars at the left curb, ignoring the RIGHT command and the green route bending right. It hit parked car 6 head-on, slowing only from 14.6 to 12.3 m/s as the gap closed from 41 m to 3.8 m.

The route went straight through the intersection (command RIGHT), but the ego turned left into the cross street at about 3.5 m/s. It drove front-first into vehicle 155, which was stopped in that street, without braking enough as the gap shrank from 9 m to 4.7 m.

With a RIGHT command at the intersection, the ego left the recorded path (which went ahead and right) and planned a path curving left toward the corner curb. It slowed from 7 to 4.4 m/s but drove onto the sidewalk by the tree at 9.3 s, about 12 m from the human trajectory. The camera view smeared only after the ego had already drifted off the recording, so the policy's own steering caused the failure.

The route command was RIGHT and the recorded path moved right, but the ego stayed in the left lanes and drifted left at about 9–10 m/s. Near the intersection it ran up onto the planted median with the palm trees and left the road, 6.3 m from the recorded path.

After handoff, the ego left its travel lane, where the recorded path runs, and steered left into the curbside lane of parked cars. It kept going at about 11-12 m/s and ran its front into parked car 6, barely slowing as the gap closed from 45 m to 4 m.

Although the route command was RIGHT, the ego kept going at about 12 m/s and drifted left across the centre line into the oncoming lane. There it collided with oncoming car 85, which was about 17 m ahead at 8.5 s and alongside the ego's left side at 9.0 s.

The ego was going about 6 m/s toward the intersection where the route turns right, with no lead car close. The offroad flag fired 1.1 s after handoff, right at the stop line. At that point the ego was only 0.5 m from the human path and still looked to be inside the mapped lanes. Its planned path was already veering left/straight instead of following the right turn, but at this moment the offroad looks marginal, possibly a corner clipping the edge of the map's drivable area at the intersection entrance.

While making the commanded right turn, the ego came in behind slow vehicle 155 in the same lane on the new road and drove into its rear. The ego sped up from 3.1 to 3.7 m/s as the gap closed from 14 m to about 5 m and barely slowed before the front collision; the recorded human path instead swung left, around 155.

The ego was at about 7 m/s, reaching the stop line of an intersection where the route turns right (the command changed from STRAIGHT to RIGHT). One second after the policy took over at 4.7 s, its planned path veered left across the intersection instead of following the right turn, and the ego was flagged offroad at 5.7 s. It was only about 0.6 m from where the human drove at that moment, so the offroad flag is marginal and may come from the ego's box clipping the drivable-area edge rather than a clear departure.

On a narrow street lined with parked cars, the ego sped up from 4.6 to 6.5 m/s and drifted left of the recorded path (about 1.4 m off). It clipped parked car 23 on the left curb with its front-left corner as it drew alongside. This was not a moving lead vehicle and the ego did not leave the road; it just held a line too close to the parked row.

While making the commanded right turn at about 4 m/s, the ego cut the corner and ended up in the parking lane on the cross street. Its front hit parked car 90, about 6.8 m off the recorded path. It also left the road around the same time, and the rear contact came only after this front collision.
